claim: Official Visit Stockholm list of currently starred restaurants — confirms Frantzén at three stars and AIRA at two stars.
quote: Frantzén earned its place in history as the first restaurant in Stockholm to earn the highly coveted third Michelin star in 2018. AIRA received its second star in 2023.

claim: Frantzén history: opened 2008, 1 star 2009, 2 stars 2010, 3 stars Feb 2018; 23 seats; current address Klara Norra Kyrkogata 26; Björn Frantzén founder.
quote: Frantzén opened in 2008 at the location of the former one-star restaurant Mistral. It earned its first Michelin star in 2009, a second star in 2010, and became the first Swedish restaurant to receive a third Michelin star in February 2018.

claim: AIRA is a 2-star Michelin restaurant by chefs Tommy Myllymäki and Pi Le, on Djurgården.
quote: AIRA is a 2-star MICHELIN restaurant by chefs Tommy Myllymäki and Pi Le.

claim: AIRA tasting menu is 3,950 SEK, 13 courses (5 appetizers, 5 mains, 3 desserts), available at lunch and dinner; wine pairings 1,100–6,500 SEK.
quote: Available lunch and dinner. Non-alcoholic pairing: 1100 SEK. Combined pairing: 1800 SEK. Wine experience: 2500 SEK. Sommelier experience: 4000 SEK. Connoisseur experience: 6500 SEK.

claim: AIRA service: Tue–Sat dinner from 18:00; Thu–Sat lunch from 12:00; address Biskopsvägen 9, 115 21 Stockholm.
quote: Tuesday – Saturday: Dinner from 18.00. Thursday – Saturday: Lunch from 12.00, dinner from 18.00.

claim: Frantzén format: roughly 10–12 courses, lounge upstairs for canapés and petit fours, main meal at a kitchen counter around an open kitchen.
quote: fixed tasting menu of roughly 10 courses. The meal begins in a casual lounge area on the top floor where canapés and dessert pastries are served, while the main meal takes place in a dining room that is really more of one giant open kitchen, ringed by a kitchen counter with stools.

claim: Frantzén capacity is 23 seats over 3 floors in a 521 m² townhouse; menu is grounded in Nordic cuisine with a touch of Japanese elegance.
quote: A set menu grounded in Nordic cuisine, with a touch of Japanese elegance. 23 seats across 3 floors in a 521 m² townhouse.

claim: Aloë held 2 stars from 2022 through 2025; Oaxen Krog reached 2 stars in 2022 but has since closed.
quote: AIRA (Nordic) - Elevated from 1 star in 2022 to 2 stars in 2023, maintaining that level through 2025. Aloë (Contemporary) - Held steady at 2 stars from 2022 through 2025. Oaxen Krog (Nordic) - Achieved 2 stars in 2022 but subsequently closed.

claim: Aloë paused operations from Feb 9 2025 for an indefinite period after co-founder Daniel Höglander died Dec 23 2024 at age 45; sister concept Rinos (basement) keeps operating.
quote: Aloë will pause operations starting February 9, 2025, for an indefinite period. Daniel Höglander died December 23, 2024, age 45. Sister restaurant Rinos, located in the basement, will continue operating normally during Aloë's closure.

claim: Frantzén dress code 'Smart and Elegant'; AIRA marked currently exclusive with advance booking essential; Aloë listed as temporarily closed.
quote: Frantzén maintains a 'Smart and Elegant' dress code, encouraging guests to dress in attire that reflects the restaurant's sophisticated ambiance. AIRA: Reservations: Exclusive; advance booking essential. Aloë: Reservations: Currently temporarily closed.

claim: The Nordic Countries 2026 Michelin Guide ceremony takes place 1 June 2026, 18:00 local time, at Tivoli Concert Hall in Copenhagen — new and lost stars will be announced then.
quote: The MICHELIN Guide Restaurant Ceremony for the Nordic Countries 2026 is set to take place on Monday 1st June at 6pm local time (GMT+2) at the Tivoli Concert Hall, set within Tivoli Gardens in Copenhagen, Denmark.

claim: Aloë is located in Älvsjö, hidden beneath a shop in a residential neighbourhood; intimate 25 seats; opened 2015; founders Daniel Höglander and Niclas Jönsson.
quote: Hidden beneath a shop in Älvsjö's residential neighborhood. Since opening in 2015, this intimate 25-seat restaurant has redefined Stockholm fine dining. Run by chefs Daniel Höglander and Niclas Jönsson.

claim: Michelin Guide page confirms Frantzén at three stars in the current Sweden guide and gives reservation/contact details.
quote: Frantzén is a three-star restaurant in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide Sweden, making it the first and only restaurant in Sweden to be awarded three stars.

claim: Frantzén reservations open on the 1st of each month at 10:00 local time for the upcoming month; tasting menu approximately 5,500 SEK per guest.
quote: Reservations for the upcoming month open on the 1st of each month at 10:00 AM local time. The menu is SEK 5,500 per guest.
